walkthroughs.body_html:
Coordinate Systems & Time — a core area of A-Level Astronomy.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Coordinate Systems & Time brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Coordinate Systems & Time.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

G2V
K5III
M0V

options: Supergiant
Giant
Main sequence
White dwarf

mcqs.q: What is the difference between an asteroid and a comet?
options: They are the same object with different names.
Comets are larger than asteroids.
Asteroids are rocky/metallic; comets contain ice that vaporises near the Sun, producing a tail.
How long a star lives.

mcqs.q: What does cosmological redshift tell us?
options: Comets are larger than asteroids.
Galaxies are receding from us due to the expansion of space.
Galaxies are turning red as they age.
Light gets tired and loses energy.
A unit of DISTANCE - the distance light travels in one year.
A unit of time.
Comets are larger than asteroids.
How long a star lives.
